benchmarks.label: Lemon Tree Hotels
benchmarks.rationale: The FY2026 third-party management and franchise fees illustrate one shared business activity. Lemon Tree also owns and leases hotels. The group margins, cash conversion and quote multiples are not peer benchmarks.

sections.question: What drives growth?
sections.finding: FY2026 operating revenue grew 49.7%. G6 supplied 73.4% of the increase in gross booking value as its first full year entered the comparison. Ex-G6 hotel bookings also grew.
sections.review_trigger: Use a full-year G6 same-store bridge and separate gross bookings from the revenue Oravel recognises.

sections.question: Is profit turning into cash?
sections.finding: Operating cash reached ₹2,511.21 crore. After cash capex, borrowing interest and lease payments, ₹408.46 crore remained versus ₹-1,038.57 crore in FY2025. Reported FY2026 PAT includes a net tax credit of ₹595.25 crore. The cash sensitivity still excludes debt principal and acquisition payments.
sections.review_trigger: Review repeatability of working-capital movements, acquisition integration and refinancing.

sections.question: Which listed benchmarks fit?
sections.finding: Lemon Tree discloses ₹73.9 crore from third-party management and franchise fees in FY2026. This benchmarks the fee model only. Oravel combines global franchise, principal hotel and home-agent revenues, and acquired G6.
sections.review_trigger: Require matched third-party franchise fee and property definitions before comparing monetisation.

sections.question: What does the quote imply?
sections.finding: The ₹20.45 dealer indication gives 30.07× reported basic EPS and about ₹30,785 crore on the draft's converted pre-issue share count. Tax credits, preference conversion and eventual new shares affect interpretation. The October addendum revises the fresh issue to up to ₹3,350 crore and earmarks ₹2,512.50 crore for borrowing repayment. The official price band remains pending.
sections.review_trigger: Refresh with executable quote terms, final capitalization, updated debt uses and the offer price.
